Mr. G.C. Sahu, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Orissa ...

Opposite Party
 Mr. K.K. Mohapatra, Advocate for the Informant
 Mr. S.S. Pradhan, Aga
 Coram:
 Justice G. Satapathy
 Order
21.06.2023 Order No.
02. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual /Physical Mode).
2.

This is an application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with G.R.
Case No.413 of 2020 arising out of Banki P.S. Case No.297 of 2020 pending in the file of learned SDJM, Banki for commission of offences punishable under Sections 406/419/120-B/420/468/471 of IPC r/w Section-66D/84C of I.T. Act, on the main allegation of cheating the informant for a sum of Rs. 1,33,000/- by impersonating himself as an employee of NABARD and obtain the pecuniary benefits in such pretext to dig a bore well for the Informant.
3.

In the course of hearing of the bail application, Mr. G.C. Sahu, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has already been sufficiently punished by remaining in jail for more than three months and in the meanwhile charge- sheet has been submitted in this case.
On these grounds, he prays to grant bail to the Petitioner.
4. On the other hand, Mr. S.S. Pradhan, learned AGA, however, strongly opposes the bail application of the Petitioner.
5. Mr. K.K. Mohapatra, learned counsel for the Informant, however, by taking through the objection of the Informant, submits to not to grant bail to the present petitioner.

sentences.text:
7. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands allowed and the petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two local solvent sureties for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail,

(ii) the petitioner shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless his attendance is dispensed with,
(iii) the petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case and It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.
In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioner for similar offences in future on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail in this case.
8. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
9. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy)
